Add "bring your own Deepgram key" (BYOK) to the Earshot **web app** in /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web (Next.js 16 App Router, Tailwind v4). Another agent is changing `apps/extension` at the same time — don't touch it, and don't edit `packages/shared` (report shared bugs instead). Don't run `npm install`, don't commit, don't touch any process on port 3000 (unrelated project). Never print API key values.

## Goal
The owner wants to deploy publicly without paying for other people's Deepgram usage. Two modes must both work:
1. **Server key mode (must keep working exactly as today):** `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` set in `apps/web/.env.local` → `POST /api/deepgram/token` mints 60 s JWTs, no key prompt ever. This is how the owner runs it locally; do not regress it.
2. **BYOK mode:** no server key → on Start, the user is asked to paste their own Deepgram API key (with a link to https://console.deepgram.com/ to sign up / create a key and a short note to create a dedicated key with minimal permissions and an expiry). The key is stored only in this browser (localStorage, wrapped in try/catch), used directly by the browser on the Deepgram WebSocket, and never sent to the Earshot server. Users can also choose to use their own key even when a server key exists (e.g. a "Use my own Deepgram key" option in settings) — when a user key is saved it takes precedence; show which mode is active.

## Already done in packages/shared (read `src/core/session.ts`, `src/core/deepgram.ts`, `src/core/types.ts`, `src/core/token.ts`)
- `TranscriptionSession({ getToken })` — `getToken` may now return `string` (bearer JWT, today's path) or `DeepgramCredential` `{ type: "token", value: userKey }`. With a user key, a handshake failure on the first connect ends the session with status `error` and a message containing "API key" (no retry loop).
- `verifyDeepgramKey(key) → Promise<"ok" | "rejected" | "offline">` (opens a socket briefly; Deepgram REST has no browser CORS so this is the only check) and `looksLikeDeepgramKey(key)`.
- `createTokenFetcher(endpoint)` throws `FatalTranscriptionError` on 401/403/500/503.

## What to build
- Server: make the token route report availability without minting: add `GET /api/deepgram/token` → `{ serverKey: boolean }` (same CORS/rate-limit handling as POST; never reveal the key). Keep POST's "no key" response a clear error (use 503 with `{ error, code: "no_server_key" }`).
- Client: small module (e.g. `src/lib/deepgram-key.ts`) for load/save/forget of the user key in localStorage (key name like `earshot:deepgram-key`) and a `getToken` factory that returns `{type:"token", value}` when a user key is saved, otherwise the server token fetcher.
- On the watch page: before capture starts, decide the mode (cache the GET result). If no server key and no user key → show a polished "Add your Deepgram key" dialog/card (input type=password with show/hide, paste-friendly, Verify & save button using `verifyDeepgramKey`, inline errors for rejected/offline/malformed, link to the console, privacy copy: "Your key stays in this browser and goes only to Deepgram"). After saving, continue straight into the normal Start flow (start guide → getDisplayMedia). Make sure the getDisplayMedia call still happens from a user click (if the dialog consumed the gesture, require the user to click Start in the guide).
- Settings popover: a "Deepgram key" section — shows "Using server key" / "Using your key (••••last4)", lets the user add/replace (verify first) or Forget their key. If an active session hits the "API key" error, surface a button that opens this section.
- Home page: if `serverKey` is false, mention in the how-it-works/privacy area that you'll need a free Deepgram key; keep it brief.
- Update `apps/web/.env.example` comments: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY is now optional (unset = visitors bring their own key).
- Match the existing dark design (ink-* + amber accent tokens, shared components).

## Verify (report real outputs)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web` and `npm run build -w @earshot/web` pass.
- Server-key mode: run the server on port 3100 (`npm run start -w @earshot/web` after build, or dev), confirm `GET /api/deepgram/token` → `{serverKey:true}`, and run the existing real-browser e2e `EARSHOT_URL=http://localhost:3100 npm run e2e -w @earshot/web` — it must PASS (headful Chrome window opens ~30 s; YouTube occasionally flakes — rerun once before concluding failure).
- BYOK mode: start a second server with the key removed from its environment (e.g. `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY= REDACTED next start -p 3101` from apps/web — check Next doesn't still load it from .env.local; if it does, temporarily point it elsewhere without editing/deleting the owner's .env.local, e.g. a copy of the built app or an env override that wins). Confirm GET → `{serverKey:false}`, POST → 503. Then extend `scripts/e2e.mjs` with an `E2E_USER_KEY` mode (read the key from env; the test runner can source it from apps/web/.env.local without printing it) that goes through the key dialog, saves the key, starts captions, and asserts transcript lines; plus a bad-key run asserting the rejected message. Run both against 3101 and report. Also check the dialog in the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* tools) at desktop and mobile widths for layout.
- Stop every server you started.

Final report: files changed, behaviour in both modes, verification outputs, anything not verified.

content.text:
BYOK now works in the web app, and server-key mode still works as before. Typecheck, build and every e2e run passed on the final build. One BYOK e2e run on `localhost:3101` needed four tries: the first three hit YouTube player error 5 before any audio played, then it passed.

## Behaviour
- **Server-key mode** (`DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` set): unchanged. `GET /api/deepgram/token` returns `{"serverKey":true}`, POST still mints 60 s JWTs, and no key prompt appears. Settings shows "Using server key" and offers "Use my own Deepgram key".
- **BYOK mode** (no server key): GET returns `{"serverKey":false}`, and POST returns 503 `{error, code:"no_server_key"}`.
  - **Start** opens an "Add your Deepgram key" dialog. It has:
    - a password input with show/hide that trims pasted keys;
    - a "Verify & save" button, using `verifyDeepgramKey`;
    - inline errors for empty, malformed, rejected and offline keys;
    - the console.deepgram.com link;
    - a tip to create a dedicated key with the Member role and an expiry;
    - "Your key stays in this browser and goes only to Deepgram."
  - After saving, the start guide always opens, so the tab-share prompt still comes from the user's click on "Choose this tab". Verifying the key uses up the original click.
- **Precedence:** a saved user key wins in both modes. The key is read on every connect, stored in localStorage as `earshot:deepgram-key` (in memory if storage is blocked), and synced across tabs.
- **Settings popover** has a new "Deepgram key" section. It shows "Using server key", "Using your key (••••last4)" or "No key yet", with buttons to add or replace (verified first) and to forget the key.
- **Key errors during a session:** if a session fails with an "API key" error, the error banner offers "Check Deepgram key", which opens that section with the form showing, plus "Restart captions". With no key at all, the button reads "Add your Deepgram key" and opens the dialog instead.
- **Home page:** when the server has no key, one line in the privacy card says a free Deepgram key is needed. This is checked in the browser, so the statically built page stays correct whatever the server's settings.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web`: passed. `npm run build -w @earshot/web`: passed (`/` static; `/api/deepgram/token` and `/watch` dynamic).
- **Mode check:** `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY= REDACTED next start -p 3101` worked. The empty value overrides `.env.local`, so I didn't need to copy or touch the owner's file.
- **Endpoints:**
  - 3100: GET returns `{"serverKey":true}`; POST returns 200 (token redacted).
  - 3101: GET returns `{"serverKey":false}`; POST returns 503 `no_server_key`.
  - Both: OPTIONS allows `GET, POST, OPTIONS`.
  - A foreign origin gets 403.
- **e2e runs:**

| Run | Port | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Server-key (existing test) | 3100 | PASS four times; 2 transcript lines, 1 server token request |
| `E2E_USER_KEY`, through the dialog | 3101 | PASS, including the 4th try on `localhost:3101`; 2 lines; key never sent to the Earshot server; 0 POSTs to the token endpoint |
| `E2E_BAD_KEY=1` | 3101 | PASS; malformed and rejected messages asserted; nothing saved |
| `E2E_USER_KEY`, through Settings, over a server key | 3100 | PASS; "Using your key", 0 server token requests |

  The last BYOK runs on `localhost:3101` hit player error 5 three times in a row. Each time it was 0 lines, status paused and no Earshot error. The same flow passed on `127.0.0.1:3101` and on 3100 straight after, then on the 4th `localhost:3101` try. I'm treating it as YouTube flakiness, but it was more than the "rerun once" you expected.
- **Rejected key mid-session** (a separate script in the scratchpad, not added to the repo): a saved fake key with capture started ends in "Deepgram didn't accept your API key…" with status error. "Check Deepgram key" opens the form, and "Forget key" clears storage. This run found that Forget was hidden while the form was open; it's fixed.
- **Built-in browser:** checked the dialog at about 800 px and at mobile 375 px, including the error state. Also checked the settings key section and the home page note. I fixed a doubled focus ring on the key input and shrank the title on phones. On phones the dialog only appears if you open it before capture is detected as unsupported, because Start is disabled on mobile.
- I stopped all four servers I started on 3100 and 3101, and port 3000 was never touched. The key was passed to the test with `$(grep …)` and never printed. The e2e log hides even the masked last 4 characters.

## Not verified
- I didn't run the `apps/extension` build or check that it compiles against these changes. Its contract with the server is unchanged: POST is the same, and the only new failure is the 503 for "no server key", which `createTokenFetcher` already treats as final (no retry).
- I didn't test the offline error for real; it's only checked in code.
- I didn't test a key changed or forgotten while captions are running beyond the code path. Settings says the change applies from the next connection.

## Issues to report (not fixed)
- **`packages/shared`:** `verifyDeepgramKey` reports any socket failure while the browser thinks it's online as "rejected", so a Deepgram outage or a blocked network looks like a bad key.
- **`packages/shared`:** in `CaptionSettingsForm`, the "Text" row slightly overflows the 20rem popover. This was already there.
- **Web app:** the global unlayered `:focus-visible` outline beats Tailwind's `focus:outline-none`, so the existing `UrlForm` input probably shows a doubled ring too. I only fixed it on the new key input.

## Files (all under `apps/web`)
- Changed:
  - `src/app/api/deepgram/token/route.ts`
  - `src/app/watch/WatchExperience.tsx`
  - `src/components/SettingsPopover.tsx` (can now be opened from outside and takes extra sections; its label is now "Settings")
  - `src/app/page.tsx`
  - `.env.example`
  - `scripts/e2e.mjs`
- New:
  - `src/lib/deepgram-key.ts`
  - `src/components/DeepgramKeyForm.tsx`
  - `src/components/DeepgramKeyDialog.tsx`
  - `src/components/DeepgramKeySettings.tsx`
